title: Сломанный туалет и запрет Вики  (The Broken Restroom and Vika's Ban)

segments.t: With the employee restroom out of order until the day after tomorrow, Vika catches Senya sneaking out of the guest bathroom in the dining room. When she forbids the cooks from using the guest facilities, Chef Barinov sarcastically asks someone to hand Vika rubber gloves so she can fix the plumbing herself.
Может, вы сюда еще всей кухней ходить будете?
Она хочет сама починить наш туалет.
Значит так, пока не починят туалет для персонала.
Now let's break down each line of their conversation.
'What are you doing out here?' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'you' before landing on 'are doing'. Vika answers right away.
'Would you like me to give you all the details?' Vika brings out the contrast between 'for you' and 'detail' in a few short words.
Может, вы сюда еще всей кухней ходить будете?
'Maybe your whole kitchen crew is going to start coming out here?' Senya anchors the line on 'maybe', while 'will be' completes the thought.
'Of course we are.' The grammar packs 'of course' and 'we will' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange. Vika answers right away.
'They will not fix it until the day after tomorrow.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'to fix' and finishing on 'the day after tomorrow'.
'You are not going to come out here anymore.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'but' before landing on 'will be'.
'Give Viktoriya Sergeyevna a pair of gloves.' The meaning hinges on 'give' working together with 'gloves' in spoken Russian. Vika answers right away.
Она хочет сама починить наш туалет.
'She wants to fix our restroom all by herself.' Notice how Russian expresses 'she' and 'restroom' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
'Wait, where is he?' Senya anchors the line on 'and', while 'he' completes the thought.
'Where is he? Are you writing this down?' Chef Viktor raises the pitch on 'write' to turn the phrase into a direct spoken question. Vika answers right away.
'What, is one hand not enough?' The grammar packs 'what' and 'little' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'Everyone is assembled.' The grammar packs 'all' and 'assembly' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
Значит так, пока не починят туалет для персонала.

'Alright then, until they fix the staff restroom.' Notice how Russian expresses 'so' and 'staff' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Now let's put it all back together and hear the whole scene again.
Может, вы сюда еще всей кухней ходить будете?
Она хочет сама починить наш туалет.
Значит так, пока не починят туалет для персонала.
